subject: Defining Lambda in occuPEN in Unmarked program

messages.author: 8e3e215dc8990323
messages.subject: Defining Lambda in occuPEN in Unmarked program
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am using occuPEN for a single season occupancy model in the Unmarked package for the first time. I have 32 sites with 3 visits, 1 site covariates, and 2 survey covariate. My data has some missing visits in detection history that matches survey covariates.  
My models are running well when I was using single season occupancy model of MacKenzie et al (2002) in the Unmarked package. Then, I tried to apply the penalized occupancy models of Hutchison et al (2015) since my sample sizes are small. However, I have some issues and/questions:
1. How to define Lambda in par.type "Ridge", "Bayes", "MPLE"? I have tried running the model without defining Lambda and by defining Lambda =1 for par.type="Ridge" and "Bayes". The models work but the SE value is NA.
2. For "MPLE", I tried to compute Lambda using computeMPLELamda in par type= "MPLE", but I got an error  "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed". I know this error appears due to missing visits in my dataset. How should I deal with this situation? 

I would really appreciate if anyone could let me know how to solve those problems in Unmarked. 

Thanks in advance!

Bayu

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Defining Lambda in occuPEN in Unmarked program
parts:
For (1) (using "Ridge" or "Bayes") you should try running occuPEN_CV (as a cross-validation approach is unnecessary for "MPLE") and use a bootstrap for estimating standard errors.  For (2) you should either forget using par.type = MPLE, drop the sites with missing values, or use a Bayesian approach.

Jim
